title: SCIM: group-merge safety, backpressure-aware retries, and deprovision audit traces
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers report rare but high-severity races when large group membership changes (enterprise group syncs) interleave with deprovision events and automated retries from IdPs. These races can cause temporary RBAC elevation (users remain in groups after deprovision), duplicate membership churn, and gaps in audit trails. This ticket implements a defensive, observable, and tenant-aware approach to SCIM group merges and deprovision retries.
acceptance_criteria: Group membership updates from SCIM must be applied in an order-safe way: concurrent merges/patches from the same identity provider and same tenant must be serializable (no lost updates).

Deprovision events must create an auditable tombstone that ties the user id, tenant, source request id, and operation id; tombstones must prevent accidental re-provision from stale retry attempts for at least 7 days.

A per-tenant backpressure and rate limiter prevents our SCIM worker pool from being overwhelmed by large delta floods; under backpressure, clients receive 429 with Retry-After header and retries are recorded in metrics.
End-to-end tests demonstrating no RBAC elevation under simulated concurrent delta streams (Okta/OneLogin/Azure AD) and a chaos scenario with intermittent DB latency.
New observability: dashboard with "SCIM apply latency", "SCIM retry rate", "tombstone rehydrate attempts", and an alert when effective group-ops/sec > tenant-configured safe threshold.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Canonical diffs and chunked apply: break large group changes into idempotent chunks (PATCH semantics) using canonical sorted member lists and deterministic chunk boundaries to reduce lost-update surface area.
2) Per-tenant sequence token: persist a monotonic SCIM apply sequence per tenant + source. Each incoming SCIM payload carries the IdP's request-id; we map request-id -> sequence token to ensure we only apply operations that are newer than the last-seen token.
3) Compare-and-swap commit: use DB transaction with optimistic CAS on tenant_sequence and membership version. If CAS fails, re-fetch and reapply diff.
4) Tombstone and TTL: on deprovision, create a tombstone record with user_id, tenant_id, source, original_request_id, operation_id, and set TTL=7d. Any incoming provisioning for that user with older timestamps or matching request_id is dropped and logged to audit.
5) Backpressure and rate limiting: token-bucket per-tenant worker queue + global admission. When queue depth exceeds threshold, return 429/Retry-After and emit metrics; implement exponential backoff policy guided by tenant-config.
6) Idempotency and dedupe: maintain small LRU cache of recent request-ids per-tenant and persist dedupe entries for 24h to avoid double-apply from identical retries.
7) Observability hooks: attach trace/span to each SCIM operation with tags: tenant, source, request_id, op_type, chunk_id, tombstone_hit=true/false. Ship structured audit event to audit-log pipeline for every decision point (apply/skip/tombstone).
test_plan: Unit tests for chunking logic, canonicalization, and CAS retry path.
Integration tests against local SCIM consumer that simulates Okta/OneLogin/Azure AD style retries and duplicate request-ids.
Load test: k6 script that replays a 200k-member group sync split into 500 PATCH chunks and verifies eventual membership correctness and per-tenant rate limiting behavior.
Chaos scenario: introduce 300-500ms DB latency on apply transactions and validate tombstone enforcement and lack of RBAC elevation.
E2E test: onboard a staging tenant with scheduled deprovision + re-provision flakiness and validate audit traces link operations to original IdP request-ids.
risks: Increased write amplification for large groups due to chunking; may raise costs for very large enterprise tenants.
Incorrect sequence/token mapping could cause legitimate out-of-order but newer operations to be dropped if timestamp semantics are mishandled.
Tombstone TTL too short may allow a delayed retry to re-create a deprovisioned account; TTL too long could confuse legitimate re-provisions.
Per-tenant rate limits could result in 429s for aggressive IdP retries which might impact customer UX; need to document expected behavior and provide tenant-config knobs.
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike completed - implemented canonical member list comparator; validated deterministic chunking in unit harness.
2025-02-12: Design review with PM/SEC. Agreed on 7d tombstone default and opt-out per-enterprise via admin UI. Security requested audit event schema and retention to be included in next PR.
2025-02-13: Implemented per-tenant sequence table and CAS flow in sandbox. Observability spans emitting but audit pipeline mapping pending.

2025-02-15: Started integration tests with Okta replay script. Found an edge where request-id collision from upstream retries lacked a unique operation_id - added operation_id derivation and dedupe persist.
